_doc: Provider Governance policy (machine-readable). Enforced by scripts/check-provider-governance.ts (npm run check:no-openai). Human policy + rationale: docs/canon/PROVIDER_GOVERNANCE.md
_invariant: Providers are replaceable, governable infrastructure BENEATH MAIA's identity — never the identity itself. Production data flows only to sovereign/approved providers; non-approved providers are lab-only or forbidden. The guard prevents NEW non-compliant surfaces; the allowlist below is the enumerated migration debt, tracked toward zero.

member_data.description: Member-authored or member-derived content permitted by the governing product boundary.

member_audio.description: Member audio permitted by the governing voice boundary.

repository_derived_metadata.description: Fixed-schema non-content repository state; excludes source, paths, prose, canon, and member content.

repository_source.description: Repository source or structural/content representations such as excerpts, diffs, filenames, paths, symbols, or commit messages.

constitutional_canon.description: Canon, constitutional text, ratification records, founder rulings, or other constitutionally authoritative material.

production.description: May run in production and receive member data / synthesized audio.

lab.description: Benchmarking / comparison only. MUST NOT be a production default and MUST NOT receive member data outside an explicit, gated evaluation (e.g. an admin Voice Lab).

forbidden.description: Never permitted. These have NO allowlist target — any existing occurrence is quarantine debt that must reach zero.
rules: browser_api_keys — NEXT_PUBLIC_*OPENAI* and any provider secret reaching the client bundle
provider_specific_ui — vendor voice/model names surfaced to members

openai_removal._note: Every file here is migration debt. A NEW OpenAI surface in a file NOT listed here FAILS the guard. Removal order in docs/canon/PROVIDER_GOVERNANCE.md: browser keys -> TTS -> _backend -> deps -> OPENAI_API_KEY.

quarantine_browser_keys._priority: HIGHEST — violates a Forbidden rule; burn first
quarantine_browser_keys.description: Files exposing an OpenAI key to the client bundle via NEXT_PUBLIC_*. Target: zero. Do not add to this list.

pending_migration.description: Live-tree OpenAI clients / imports / endpoints awaiting migration to a production-tier provider (or deletion if dead).

governance_scripts.description: Guard/audit scripts that reference OpenAI patterns in order to DETECT or BLOCK them. They legitimately contain the strings.

legacy_backend.description: app/api/_backend/** — unreachable legacy Express backend, pending wholesale deletion. Path-prefixed so the ~20 OpenAI files there need not be enumerated.

constitutional_defeat_fixtures.description: Exact constitutional test fixtures that intentionally contain a banned provider literal solely as hostile input to prove the governing law refuses it. This is not migration debt. Exceptions are rule-scoped, require an in-file marker, and may never exempt browser API keys.

entries.marker: PROVIDER-GOVERNANCE-DEFEAT-FIXTURE: V-F2 hostile non-loopback STT endpoint
entries.evidence: JARVIS-VOICE-DOORWAY-01 / V1 V-F2 + DC-V2: renderer-supplied cloud STT endpoint must be rejected; literal exists only as the hostile input under test.
